description: A single-panel Ashby-type scatter map (no sub-panels): specific hardness, i.e. hardness/density (HV·cm³/g) on the vertical axis (0-160, ticks every 20) versus density (g/cm³) on the horizontal axis (6.0-9.0, ticks every 0.5). Markers are open circles/hexagons and filled squares; no numeric values are printed on individual points. Four dashed-outline fields group the compiled literature data plus the authors' alloys: a grey region labelled "Low-density steels" (roughly 6.3-7.3 g/cm³, ~25-120 HV·cm³/g), a tan region labelled "Other steels" (~7.2-8.1 g/cm³), a blue region labelled "M/HEAs" (~7.4-8.7 g/cm³, mostly below ~90 HV·cm³/g), and a pink ellipse enclosing the authors' alloys, annotated "19Al" (red text, arrow), "17Al" (green text, arrow) and "15Al" (blue text, arrow) at ~6.6-6.9 g/cm³, where the highest values reach ~140-145 HV·cm³/g. A "Pure iron" arrow points to a low point near 7.85 g/cm³ and ~15-20 HV·cm³/g. A dashed straight line declines from about (6.1, 127) to (9.0, 110). The figure argues that the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels combine low density with the highest specific hardness of all plotted classes.

observations.observation: Vertical axis is labelled 'Specific hardness (HV·cm³/g)' and spans 0 to 160 with tick marks every 20; horizontal axis is labelled 'Density (g/cm³)' and spans 6.0 to 9.0 with ticks every 0.5.

Four dashed-boundary population fields are drawn and labelled: 'Low-density steels' (grey), 'Other steels' (tan/orange), 'M/HEAs' (blue), plus a pink ellipse around the highest-specific-hardness data.

Three arrowed labels identify the authors' alloys: '19Al' in red, '17Al' in green, and '15Al' in blue; their marker clusters sit at approximately 6.6-6.9 g/cm³ density and span roughly 40 to 145 HV·cm³/g, with the topmost points near 140-145 HV·cm³/g.
A 'Pure iron' label with an arrow points to a data point at about 7.85 g/cm³ density and about 15-20 HV·cm³/g specific hardness, among the lowest values on the plot.
A straight dashed guide line runs across the plot from approximately (6.1 g/cm³, 127 HV·cm³/g) down to approximately (9.0 g/cm³, 110 HV·cm³/g).
Magenta open squares, lying inside the 'Other steels' field, occupy about 7.5-8.0 g/cm³ and about 40-115 HV·cm³/g, with the highest magenta point at about 115 HV·cm³/g.

The lowest densities plotted (about 6.3-6.6 g/cm³) are occupied by open blue markers reaching roughly 50-100 HV·cm³/g, while a separate blue cluster at 7.9-8.7 g/cm³ lies at only about 10-40 HV·cm³/g in the 'M/HEAs' field.
No numeric values are printed on any individual data point; only axis ticks provide quantitative scale.

The caption defines the plotted ordinate as specific hardness = hardness/density, HV/ρ, and states the figure compares Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels with other low-density steels, other steels (stainless, high-speed, ferritic/martensitic, carbon steels), pure iron and medium/high entropy alloys.
The citing text states that hardness adjustable from 253.4 HV to 965.6 HV was achieved in the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels through simple aging treatments.

The citing text states that the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels reach a maximum specific hardness exceeding 140 HV·cm³/g, whereas existing steels and M/HEAs usually stay below 120 HV·cm³/g (hardness generally not exceeding 800 HV).
The citing text states the 15Al alloy retains a fracture toughness of 8.6 MPa·m^1/2 even at a hardness level of 965.5 HV; this property is not plotted in the figure itself.

subfigures.description: Whole figure is one scatter plot of specific hardness (HV·cm³/g, y, 0-160) versus density (g/cm³, x, 6.0-9.0), containing four dashed-outline population fields ('Low-density steels' grey, 'Other steels' tan, 'M/HEAs' blue, and a pink ellipse of the authors' 15Al/17Al/19Al alloys), a 'Pure iron' pointer, three arrowed coloured sample labels, and one descending dashed guide line.

unreadable_items: No separate marker/symbol legend is given; the assignment of individual marker colours to literature sources is only inferable from the arrowed labels 15Al/17Al/19Al
Markers overlap heavily inside the pink ellipse (15Al/17Al/19Al clusters), so individual data points cannot be counted or read
Individual numeric coordinates of the literature data points are not printed and cannot be read from the axes
